P.V. Sindhu beats Chiu Pin-Chian to storm into French Open semifinals
 The Indian will meet either fifth seed Putri Wardani of Indonesia or Hina Akechi of Japan in the last-four stage.

 P.V. Sindhu beat Chinese Taipei’s Chiu Pin-Chian 21-13, 21-14 to reach the women’s singles semifinals of the French Open on Friday.
 Sindhu began confidently and took the opening game 21-13, keeping Chiu on the back foot for most of the game.
 ALSO READ
 Nozomi Okuhara survives Ashmita Chaliha scare to win French Open quarterfinal in three games
 She carried that control into the second, waltzing to an 11-2 lead at the interval. Chiu showed semblance of a fightback, but Sindhu closed it 21-14.
 Earlier, the double Olympic medallist sailed into the quarterfinals with a straight-game win over Japan’s Riko Gunji, prevailing 21-12, 21-16 in 44 minutes.
 Before that, the Indian made heavy weather of beating Supanida Katethong 21-14, 8-21, 23-21. She lost 11 points in a row when two points away from victory, but prevailed in the end.
 Sindhu will next face Japan’s Hina Akechi, a left-handed former junior world No. 1 who won her first BWF World Tour title at the Syed Modi International in November last year.
 Akechi defeated Indonesia’s Putri Kusuma Wardani 21-17, 21-18 in the quarterfinals of the French Open 2026.
 Akechi is known for tactical discipline and patience in long rallies, which will test Sindhu’s patience as much as her power.
